# Disposable updater ZIP fixtures

These are independent Python standard-library `zipfile` ZIP_STORED bytes, not
archives generated by the reader under test. `generate.py` sets explicit Unix
file/symlink attributes and a fixed ZIP timestamp. `truncated.zip` retains only
the first 40 bytes of `plain.zip`, omitting the central directory. The manifest
records the exact archive, signature and public-key SHA-256 values and entry
names. No fixture contains an `.exe` or `.msi` entry.

Signatures use OpenSSL Ed25519 over the BLAKE2b-512 payload digest (minisign ED),
plus the global Ed25519 signature over the payload signature and trusted comment.
The public key/signature documents are base64 encoded as the plugin expects.
Each run generates an independent throwaway key in a temporary directory, removes
it on completion, and retains only public material. No production key is read or
needed. Public plugin `Update::verify` tests independently validate this format.
The unversioned signature covers the same valid bytes without a `version:` field.

Committed fixtures were generated on 2026-10-25; the generator command, selected
OpenSSL identity, source hashes and results are in the dated portable verification
summary; exact raw command/environment/output receipts remain privately under
ignored `.work/zip9/private-evidence`.
Regenerating gives identical ZIP bytes and new public keys/signatures:

```sh
python3 desktop/src-tauri/tests/fixtures/update-zip/generate.py \
  --output .work/updater-fixtures
```

Python 3 and OpenSSL with Ed25519 support are required. `ABBEY_ZIP_OPENSSL` can
select a supported executable when a wrapper's PATH selects an older system
OpenSSL. The native PowerShell runner resolves and passes this path explicitly;
absence/incompatibility fails the test rather than counting as a skip/pass.

| Case | Encoded behavior | Evidence consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain | harmless root text | cached public API verification only |
| parent | `../../outside/parent.txt` | native plugin child |
| outward-link | symlink to `../../outside`, then entry through it | native plugin child |
| chained-link | two archive-contained symlinks then entry through them | native plugin child |
| truncated | valid signature over truncated ZIP | native plugin child |
| preexisting-link | file through already-existing `existing` path | exact ZIP9 library contract only |
| absolute, drive-relative | generated at runtime using disposable local drive root | native plugin child |

Native Windows tests generate absolute and drive-relative path bytes and fresh
signatures inside the parent's disposable root. They refuse UNC/device sandbox
roots. The child's cwd is `outside` on the same drive, and its TEMP/TMP is a
private sibling beneath the parent root. Before constructing the updater, the
child requires the OS-resolved canonical temp/cwd to equal those private
directories and refuses linked/reparse layouts explicitly as UNEXECUTED; setting
TEMP/TMP alone is insufficient. Thus even a vulnerable reader's encoded
escape targets stay inside that root. Outside sentinels must remain identical;
new files, directories or links there fail. Each actual-plugin child must finish
within 30 seconds, verify its signature, and return the ZIP extraction error.
A signature error or merely finding no installer is not accepted as ZIP proof.

The public plugin always creates a fresh, random extraction directory. It has no
deterministic hook for seeding a pre-existing symlink/junction. Those cases call
the exact resolved ZIP9 library separately, without copying extraction logic.
The Unix symlink contract is runnable on macOS; Windows symlinks/junctions require
native Windows and suitable privilege. This does not qualify a same-user race in
the plugin temp directory, POSIX SUID/SGID/chmod semantics, Windows ACL behavior,
or a real installer/update/restart workflow.
